costGuide.title: SEAT CNHA Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a SEAT CNHA typically takes 8-11 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent specialist) due to standard transverse inline-4 packaging and ancillary removal requirements .

failures.title: SEAT CNHA Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: AdBlue System & NOx Sensor Faults - 2013-2020 models
items.whatHappens: The Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) system is prone to dosing pump failures, crystallised AdBlue in the injector, or faulty NOx sensors. This triggers warning lights and, eventually, a countdown to a no-start condition if the fault is not addressed.
items.repairVsReplace: The dosing pump or sensors can often be replaced independently. However, if the DPF has become heavily contaminated with AdBlue fluid or soot due to prolonged fault neglect, a full SEAT CNHA replacement may be the most reliable long-term solution. Read our full DPF failure guide .

items.title: DPF Clogging (Urban Use)
items.whatHappens: Frequent short, low-speed journeys prevent the Diesel Particulate Filter from reaching the temperatures required for active regeneration. This leads to progressive soot accumulation, restricted exhaust flow, loss of power, and eventual limp mode.
items.repairVsReplace: While forced regenerations or chemical cleans can temporarily resolve mild clogging, a heavily blocked DPF often requires replacement. If the blockage has caused excessive backpressure, it can damage the turbocharger, making a full engine replacement more economical.

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks
items.whatHappens: The Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) cooler can develop internal cracks, allowing coolant to mix with exhaust gases or enter the intake manifold. This manifests as unexplained coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and potential hydrolock risk if severe.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the EGR cooler is a standard repair. However, if coolant ingestion has already caused hydraulic lock and bent connecting rods, a full SEAT CNHA replacement is mandatory.

failures.goodYearsLine: As a Gen 3 EA288 architecture engine, the CNHA is generally considered significantly more reliable than the preceding EA189 generation, with fewer catastrophic timing chain or injector failures, provided the emissions systems are maintained .

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement SEAT CNHA - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used SEAT CNHA is only advisable if it comes with a comprehensive service history proving timely oil changes and, ideally, documented AdBlue system and DPF maintenance. Given the age of these engines, a low-mileage used unit is the absolute bare minimum requirement to avoid inheriting imminent emissions system faults. Explore our used engine network .

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned SEAT CNHA is the recommended choice for most owners. A reputable specialist will verify the AdBlue dosing module, NOx sensors, and DPF health, and replace all critical seals. This effectively resets the engine's reliability clock while retaining the correct TDI Ultra mapping. View reconditioned SEAT CNHA options .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the block or cylinder head has suffered damage (e.g., from hydrolock due to an EGR cooler leak). Ensure the rebuilder verifies the block's straightness and uses updated emissions components to prevent recurrence. Discuss a custom SEAT CNHA rebuild .

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Opting for a supply-and-fit service through our network ensures the replacing garage assumes full responsibility for both the unit and the labour, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty for complete peace of mind. Get a supply & fit quote .
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The SEAT CNHA was fitted to popular models like the Leon and Ateca, which typically hold retained values between £5,000 and £20,000 depending on age, mileage, and condition . While replacement costs are significant, they generally remain well within the vehicle's retained value, making a professional engine replacement a financially viable and sensible alternative to scrapping a well-maintained SEAT.

items.question: How much does a SEAT CNHA engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned SEAT CNHA engine typically costs between £2,800 and £4,500 for supply-only, with fully fitted prices ranging from £3,320 to £5,215. Pricing is estimated using the VW/Audi EA288 2.0 TDI as a baseline proxy, as the CNHA is the SEAT-specific designation of the same physical engine. Labour typically takes 8-11 hours due to standard transverse inline-4 packaging and ancillary removal requirements. Used units start around £1,200 but carry significant risk of inheriting AdBlue or DPF faults.

items.question: What is the most common SEAT CNHA engine failure?
items.answer: The dominant failures are AdBlue system faults (NOx sensors, dosing pump) and DPF clogging from urban use, typically manifesting between 80,000 and 180,000 miles. The Selective Catalytic Reduction system is prone to dosing pump failures or crystallised AdBlue in the injector, triggering warning lights and eventual no-start countdowns. Frequent short, low-speed journeys prevent the DPF from reaching regeneration temperatures, leading to progressive soot accumulation and limp mode. EGR cooler leaks are also reported at higher mileages, which can cause unexplained coolant loss or, in severe cases, hydrolock damage.

items.question: Which SEAT models use the CNHA engine?
items.answer: The SEAT CNHA was widely fitted as the efficient, high-torque 150hp diesel option across the brand's core lineup, specifically powering the Leon Mk3 (5F) and Ateca Mk1 (KH7) 2.0 TDI 150 badges. Production spanned from 2013 (Leon) and 2016 (Ateca) through 2020, serving as the primary diesel powerplant for the 150hp model designation. It was never fitted to entry-level 1.6 TDI models or higher-output 184hp FR/Cupra variants, which use different engine codes.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned SEAT CNHA engine?
items.answer: A properly reconditioned SEAT CNHA is strongly recommended over a used unit for this specific engine. A quality reconditioned unit will have the AdBlue dosing module, NOx sensors, and DPF verified or replaced, preventing the immediate recurrence of the engine's most common faults. Used units are a gamble; without documented proof of emissions system maintenance, you risk inheriting imminent AdBlue or DPF failures that can trigger no-start conditions. The cost difference is justified by the comprehensive 12-24 month warranty that accompanies a reconditioned unit.

items.question: How do I confirm my car has the CNHA engine code?
items.answer: You can verify the CNHA engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet, your V5C registration document, or the physical stamp on the engine block. The code is typically stamped on a machined pad near the oil filter housing or on the cylinder head. Do not confuse it with the CRKB (115hp) or CUNA (184hp); the "CNHA" designation is critical, as it denotes the specific 150hp TDI Ultra calibration. If you are unsure, our registration lookup tool will confirm your exact engine code before any quotes are generated.
